sate.definition: to satisfy fully or to excess
sentences: Three helpings sated an appetite that a week of walking had built.
Nothing sated his curiosity about the archive except the archive itself.
The market was satiated within a year and the second factory never opened.
Satiated with sequels, audiences returned to the original and made it a hit again.

satire.definition: humor used to expose folly or vice
sentences: The satire was so accurate that its targets quoted it approvingly.
Satire dies when reality outpaces it, which happens increasingly often.
The satirical magazine outlived four of the governments it mocked.
A satirical intent is no defense if nobody detects it.
The market was saturated before the third competitor had finished its logo.
Rain saturated the ground and the match was abandoned before the toss.
His saturnine manner concealed genuine kindness and a very dry wit.
Saturnine comes from Saturn, whose astrological influence was supposed to make you gloomy.

savant.definition: a learned person or one with exceptional ability
sentences: The savant could name the day of the week for any date in four centuries.
Being called a savant is a compliment with a slight distance built in.
He savored the correction for a full week before publishing it.
Savor the win, said the coach, meaning until Tuesday's training.
A savvy negotiator conceded the loud points and kept the quiet ones.
Politically savvy and technically clueless is a common and expensive combination.
The scabbard was more valuable than the sword it had held for centuries.
The word survives in museums and in metaphors about drawn weapons.
The method does not scale: what works for nine people fails for nine hundred.
They scaled the wall in four minutes and were arrested in five.
Scant evidence supported a claim that four newspapers repeated as fact.
He gave scant attention to the appendix, which contained the entire problem.
Skilled welders were scarce and the whole schedule bent around four of them.
Time is the only genuinely scarce resource in any project.
A scathing internal memo was leaked and read more widely than the report.
The scathing review is framed in the theater's lobby, which is either brave or clever.
The office watched the rival's collapse with undisguised schadenfreude.
German supplies the word because English politely pretends not to need it.
The scheme required nine things to go right and eight of them did.
In Britain a scheme is a plan; in America it is usually a fraud.
The schism over a single word divided the church for four centuries.
The schism began with a procedural vote and ended with two buildings.
There was not a scintilla of evidence and a great deal of confidence.
A scintilla of doubt is enough in a criminal court and nowhere else.
Scintillating in company and monosyllabic on paper, he never wrote the book.
The conversation was scintillating and nobody could reconstruct a word of it afterward.
Experts scoffed at the idea for a decade and cited it in the eleventh year.
He scoffed at the warning and bought the umbrella an hour later.
Her scorn for the proposal was expressed entirely by one raised eyebrow.
Public scorn is survivable; professional scorn ends careers quietly.

screed.definition: a long, tedious piece of writing
sentences: The screed ran to nine pages and made one reasonable point on page eight.
A screed differs from an essay mainly in the absence of an editor.
Scrupulous attribution in the footnotes made the plagiarism claim collapse.
He was scrupulous about expenses and vague about everything else.
Nobody scrutinized the assumption until it had cost four million.
She scrutinized the contract for two hours and found the clause in the last minute.
A scurvy trick, said the letter, which was written in 1811 and reads perfectly today.
The disease and the insult share a root in "scurf," meaning scaly and unpleasant.
She looked at him searchingly and he explained rather more than he had planned.
The report examines the failure searchingly and stops short of naming anyone.

secrete.definition: to produce and discharge; to hide
sentences: The plant secretes a resin that seals its own wounds.
He secreted the letters in a drawer that the executors found immediately.
The secular state pays for the cathedral's roof, which nobody finds odd anymore.
A secular argument for the sabbath is simply that people need one day off.
The lecture worked as a sedative on an audience that had eaten well.
A mild sedative before the flight was less effective than the delay announcement.

sediment.definition: matter that settles at the bottom
sentences: Sediment in the lake preserves a record of every fire in the valley.
The sediment of old grievances settles and gets stirred up by any new one.
The pamphlet was charged with sedition and outsold every legal publication that year.
Sedition laws are written broadly and enforced selectively, which is their function.
Sedulous checking of the references saved the paper from an embarrassing retraction.
He was a sedulous apprentice who became an unbearable master.
It was not seemly to celebrate before the other party had conceded.
A seemly interval between the funeral and the sale is a matter of local opinion.

seethe.definition: to be violently agitated or furious
sentences: He seethed through the meeting and wrote nothing down.
The market seethed for a week and settled two percent above where it started.
The disagreement was semantic and cost four hours anyway.
Semantic drift is why "awful" once meant full of awe.
Order was restored, or a semblance of it, by Thursday afternoon.
They maintained a semblance of partnership for the sake of one contract.
The sensational headline was corrected in a sentence nine days later.
Sensational coverage of the trial made the appeal inevitable.
The sententious final paragraph ruined an otherwise excellent essay.
Sententious advice is the sort that comes with a raised finger.
Whether the system is sentient is a question its marketing department enjoys leaving open.
Sentient beings feel; sapient ones reason, and the words are constantly confused.
He kept the broken watch for sentimental reasons and never had it repaired.
The film is sentimental in the last ten minutes and unforgivable for it.
The lighthouse stood sentinel over a coastline it could not entirely save.
A sentinel species warns you about the water before the tests do.
The seraphic smile on the toddler preceded a spectacular act of destruction.
Seraphim are the highest order of angels, which sets the bar for the adjective.
The serendipitous discovery came from a contaminated dish nobody had thrown out.
Serendipitous meetings happen most often to people who leave the house.

serendipity.definition: the luck of finding good things unsought
sentences: Libraries are engines of serendipity: you find the book beside the one you wanted.
Horace Walpole coined serendipity in 1754 from a Persian fairy tale.
She was serene through the whole hearing and furious in the car.
The serene lake at dawn is why anyone tolerates the campsite.
The serenity of the reading room ends the moment the radiators start.
Serenity in a crisis is usually a decision made much earlier.
The company severed ties with a supplier it had used for forty years.
One storm severed the only cable and the island was offline for nine days.

sextant.definition: an instrument for measuring angles in navigation
sentences: A sextant, a clock, and a table of stars located a ship to within a mile.
The sextant survives on lifeboats because it needs no power at all.

sham.definition: something false pretending to be genuine
sentences: The consultation was a sham and the decision had been minuted in March.
The whole marriage was a sham and the visa was real.
A shard of pottery dated the entire settlement two centuries earlier.
Shards of the windscreen were still turning up in the boot a year later.
The sherbet between courses is meant to clear the palate and mainly delays dinner.
Sherbet comes from an Arabic word for a cold drink, which it originally was.
He never shirked the boring parts, which is why he was trusted with the interesting ones.
Shirking is easiest in a team large enough that nobody counts.
The debate grew shrill in its second hour and useless in its third.
Calling an argument shrill is often a way of avoiding it.
A sibilant whisper carried further across the hall than speech would have.
The line is deliberately sibilant, which is why it sounds like the sea.
The siege lasted eleven months and ended over a question of water.
The office was under siege from journalists who had nothing to do until Monday.

simper.definition: to smile in a silly, affected way
sentences: He simpered at the compliment and everyone present wished he had not.
A simper is a smile that is asking for something.
The reconstruction is a simulacrum: correct in every detail and dead in all of them.
A simulacrum of consultation was performed with three emails and a survey.
Simultaneous discovery is common and priority disputes follow within months.
The two announcements were simultaneous, which nobody believed was coincidence.

sinecure.definition: a position requiring little or no work
sentences: The chairmanship was a sinecure until the scandal made it the hardest job there.
Sinecure means "without care," which describes the duties precisely.
She showed a singular gift for asking the question everyone had avoided.
It was a singular achievement in a field that rewards teams.
The sinuous road up the pass adds nine miles and every good view.
Her sinuous argument arrived somewhere unexpected and entirely earned.
The skeptic in the room asked for the raw data and ended the presentation.
A skeptic doubts the claim; a cynic doubts the person.
The skill took nine years to acquire and eleven seconds to demonstrate.
Skill is what remains when enthusiasm has been exhausted.

skirt.definition: to avoid dealing with; to pass around
sentences: The report skirts the one question everybody bought it to have answered.
The path skirts the lake and adds a mile to avoid two hundred yards of mud.
Investors were skittish for a fortnight after the first bad quarter.
The skittish horse bolted at a plastic bag and ignored a passing train.
Some skullduggery with the seating plan put the two rivals at opposite ends.
The election was decided by skullduggery that took four years to document.
Slack enforcement made the rule a suggestion within a year.
There was no slack in the schedule, which is why one delay ruined everything.

slake.definition: to satisfy a thirst or desire
sentences: Nothing slaked their curiosity until the archive released the final box.
Slaked lime is what you get when quicklime's thirst for water is satisfied.

slander.definition: a false spoken statement damaging reputation
sentences: The slander was repeated in four counties before a correction was printed anywhere.
Slander is spoken and libel is written, which lawyers care about and nobody else does.
The slapdash repair held for a decade, which was nobody's plan.
A slapdash first draft is far better than an unwritten perfect one.
The dragon is slain in the third act and the interesting part is over.
The comedian slayed the room, which is the same verb doing very different work.
The accounting was a sleight of hand that took auditors four years to see.
Sleight of hand relies on attention, not speed, which magicians hate explaining.
A slew of complaints arrived on the same morning, which suggested coordination.
The word comes from Irish and has nothing to do with slaying.
He felt slighted by an omission that was, in fact, a printing error.
Slighting the caretaker in a speech is the most expensive economy in any organization.
A slothful afternoon produced the solution that four busy weeks had not.
Sloth, the animal, moves slowly to save energy, which is not laziness but strategy.
Slovenly record-keeping meant the defense could not disprove anything.
The slovenly workshop produced immaculate work, which offended the inspector deeply.
The response was sluggish for two days and frantic on the third.
A sluggish river drops its sediment and eventually builds a delta.

sluice.definition: to wash with a flow of water
sentences: They sluiced the deck twice a day, which is why the boards lasted eighty years.
Rain sluiced the dust off the leaves and out of the air.

smattering.definition: a slight superficial knowledge or small amount
sentences: He had a smattering of Italian and the confidence of a native.
A smattering of applause greeted a speech that deserved silence.
The smug reply to a fair question turned the whole room against him.
Being right does not entitle you to be smug, though it makes it very tempting.
A snide aside about her degree was overheard and repeated for years.
Snide criticism is the kind that can be denied afterward.
He was snubbed at the reception and mentioned it for a decade.
Snubbing a rival in public costs nothing and earns a permanent enemy.
She sobbed for a minute, apologized, and finished the presentation.
The sob story in the appeal letter was entirely true, which made it harder to read.
The sobriquet stuck for forty years and outlived the incident that caused it.
"The Iron Chancellor" is a sobriquet that has been applied to at least four people.

solecism.definition: a grammatical error or social blunder
sentences: The solecism in the first line of the invitation was noticed by everybody.
Solecism is named after Soloi, a colony whose Greek the Athenians found appalling.
The solicitous nurse checked four times and the patient slept through all of them.
His solicitous enquiries about her health began the week she was promoted.
Her solicitude for the junior staff was the department's only real management.
Excessive solicitude can be a burden dressed as kindness.
Solidarity lasted until the first individual offer was made.
The gesture of solidarity cost nothing and mattered enormously.

soliloquy.definition: a speech made alone, revealing thoughts
sentences: The soliloquy tells the audience what the character will not say to anyone else.
His soliloquy in the meeting lasted twelve minutes and answered no questions.
The charity remained solvent through the crisis on the strength of one legacy.
Barely solvent for two years, the firm was suddenly and briefly profitable.
The somatic symptoms were real regardless of what had caused them.
Somatic cells make up the body; germ cells make the next one.
The somber mood in the hall preceded the announcement by half an hour.
The somber palette of the painting is mostly the varnish, which will be removed.
The somnolent afternoon session lost half its audience to the corridor.
A somnolent village in August wakes up entirely for the fete.
His sonorous voice made even the disclaimers sound important.
The sonorous bell can be heard four villages away on a still night.
The sophisticated model failed for a reason the crude one had built in.
Sophisticated once meant adulterated, which is a strange origin for a compliment.
The defense was sophistry of a high order and the jury saw through it in an hour.
Sophistry differs from error in knowing better.
The soporific effect of the third speaker was visible from the back row.
Beatrix Potter noted that lettuce is soporific, which is medically dubious and charming.
The sordid details filled four pages and the significant ones filled none.
A sordid little dispute about expenses ended a distinguished career.

sound.definition: solid, reliable, and free of defect
sentences: The building is structurally sound and aesthetically indefensible.
His reasoning was sound and his premises were invented.
The sky was spangled with stars the city dwellers had never seen.
A costume spangled beyond reason survives in the museum's least visited case.
He was sparing with praise, which made it worth something when it came.
Be sparing with adjectives and the nouns do more work.
Attendance was sparse and the speaker gave the talk of her life anyway.
Sparse data invites confident interpretation, which is the danger.
The spartan accommodation had one blanket and a view worth four hotels.
Sparta's austerity gave English an adjective and very little literature.
The spat over a parking space escalated into a boundary dispute.
A spat between two departments closed a corridor for eleven months.

spate.definition: a sudden large number of things
sentences: A spate of resignations in one week told the story the accounts had not.
A river in spate is fast, brown, and not to be crossed.
She spearheaded the campaign and let four other people take the podium.
The project was spearheaded by someone who left before it delivered.
The specious argument survived because checking it required reading the appendix.
Specious originally meant simply beautiful, which explains the trap in the word.
A spectral figure in the photograph turned out to be a curtain and a long exposure.
The spectral quality of the fog made the familiar street unrecognizable.

spectrum.definition: a full range of related qualities
sentences: Opinion covered the whole spectrum, which is why no decision emerged.
The spectrum of light from a distant star reveals what it is made of.

speculate.definition: to guess without firm evidence; to invest riskily
sentences: It is idle to speculate, he said, and then speculated for nine minutes.
He speculated in property, which is a respectable word for gambling with a roof.
The spendthrift heir emptied in eleven years what four generations had built.
One spendthrift in a household outspends three savers.
The splenetic letter to the editor was signed only "Disgusted."
The spleen was thought to produce ill humor, which is where the word comes from.
Sporadic gunfire continued for a week after the ceasefire was announced.
His attendance was sporadic and his contributions, when he came, were decisive.
A sportive remark in the middle of the eulogy was exactly what the room needed.
The otters' sportive behavior is, biologists insist, also practice for hunting.
The spurious correlation between the two series was quoted in three papers.
A spurious quotation attributed to Churchill circulates every election.
He spurned the offer publicly and negotiated privately for a better one.
She spurned every attempt at reconciliation until the last one.
The squalid conditions were documented in 1888 and improved by about 1930.
A squalid little argument about credit ruined a genuine achievement.
He lived in squalor and left an estate worth four million.
The squalor of the accommodation was raised at every inspection and never fixed.
They squandered a two-goal lead and a decade of goodwill in ninety minutes.
He squandered the inheritance carefully, over twenty years, on genuinely interesting failures.
The squeamish should skip chapter four, which the author says on page one.
He was squeamish about blood and entirely unmoved by the accounts.
Management squelched the rumor and confirmed it a fortnight later.
One sharp question squelched an argument that had run for two meetings.
The staid old firm hired a designer and everyone panicked for a quarter.
Staid is respectable with the excitement removed.

stake.definition: something risked or an interest held
sentences: Everyone with a stake in the outcome was on the committee, which explained everything.
The stakes were high and the discussion was about the font.
A stalwart of the committee for thirty years, she missed one meeting and it collapsed.
Stalwart supporters are the ones who turn up in the rain.
Nothing stanched the flow of departures until the manager was replaced.
He stanched the bleeding with a shirt and drove one-handed to the hospital.
Her standing in the field was built on two papers and thirty years of refereeing.
The claim was dismissed because the plaintiff had no legal standing.

stanza.definition: a group of lines in a poem
sentences: The final stanza reverses everything the first four have established.
Stanza is Italian for room, which is a lovely way to think about a poem.
The stark contrast between the two districts fits on one page of the report.
The stark white room was designed to be calming and achieved the opposite.
She started at the sound and spilled coffee across the entire draft.
He started awake at four and lay there rehearsing the meeting.

stasis.definition: a state of inactivity or standstill
sentences: The department existed in stasis for four years between two reorganizations.
Stasis is not peace; it is a fight nobody has the energy to have.
Wages were static for six years while everything else was not.
The static image on the screen was a frozen video and nobody noticed for ten minutes.
A staunch defender of the library, she attended every hearing for nine years.
Staunch allies are identified in a crisis and never in a survey.
Steadfast in the face of ridicule, he was proved right in the fourth decade.
Steadfast and stubborn differ only in the outcome.
The tea steeps for four minutes and no argument about it is welcome.
He was steeped in the tradition before he could name any part of it.
The town is steeped in a history it prints on tea towels.
Steeped in the literature, she could cite the objection before it was made.

stem.definition: to stop or restrain the flow
sentences: Nothing stemmed the tide of resignations until the pay review.
Stem from means to originate; stem the tide means to stop it. Same word, opposite jobs.

stentorian.definition: extremely loud and powerful, of a voice
sentences: His stentorian delivery reached the back of the hall and startled the front.
Stentor was a Greek herald said to be as loud as fifty men.
A stern letter from the regulator changed a policy that four reports had not.
Stern in public and indulgent in private describes most grandparents.

stevedore.definition: a dock worker who loads ships
sentences: The stevedores' strike stopped a port that fed three counties.
Containerization replaced ten thousand stevedores with four cranes.
The culture stifled dissent so effectively that the warnings arrived only in exit interviews.
She stifled a laugh at exactly the wrong moment in the ceremony.
The stigma attached to the diagnosis kept people from testing for a decade.
Stigma was originally a brand burned onto slaves and criminals.
Policies that stigmatize the users reduce uptake and are then called unpopular.
He was stigmatized for a mistake that four colleagues had made unpunished.
The stilted dialogue in the first act loosens considerably in the second.
Their stilted exchange in the corridor confirmed the rumor immediately.
The stingy portion sizes were the restaurant's most reviewed feature.
He was stingy with money and extravagant with time, which is the rarer generosity.

stint.definition: to be sparing or restrict supply
sentences: They did not stint on the materials, which is why the roof is still there.
The organizers stinted on chairs and everybody remembers it.
Her praise was unstinting, which in that department was almost eccentric.
A stinting budget produced a stinting result, to everyone's feigned surprise.
The stipend covered rent and left nothing for the books the course required.
A modest stipend and a good library have produced most of the best work in the field.
The will stipulated that the house could never be sold, which lawyers eventually undid.
The contract stipulates a response within five days and specifies no penalty.
He gave the stock answer, which nobody believed and everybody accepted.
The film relies on stock characters and one genuinely surprising ending.
He was stoic about the diagnosis and furious about the parking charges.
Stoic philosophy is about what you control, which is less than you think and more than you fear.
The stolid clerk processed the crisis with the same face he used for holidays.
Stolid endurance is undervalued until the week it is all that remains.
Give me a straight answer, she said, and received a straight answer eventually.
A straight dealer in a crooked market rarely lasts and is always remembered.

stratagem.definition: a clever scheme to gain advantage
sentences: The stratagem worked once and was expected every time thereafter.
A stratagem is a plan that assumes an opponent.

stratum.definition: a layer, especially social or geological
sentences: Each stratum in the cliff face represents about four thousand years.
The scheme benefited one stratum and was described as universal.
The striate rock face records the passage of a glacier that left ten thousand years ago.
Striated muscle looks banded under a microscope, which is how it got the name.
The strictures of the funding body shaped the research more than any theory.
His strictures on the draft filled three pages and improved it enormously.
Years of internal strife did more damage than any competitor managed.
Industrial strife in that decade produced both the worst service and the best pay deal.
Stringent testing delayed the launch by a year and prevented a recall.
The stringent criteria excluded almost everyone the scheme was designed for.
He strutted through the office for a week after the mention in the newsletter.
The pigeon strutted across the terrace as though it owned the building, which it effectively did.
Endless process stultified a team that had been genuinely inventive.
The stultifying routine was defended as stability.
The question stumped four experts and was answered by a first-year student.
He was stumped for a name he had known for twenty years.
A stupendous effort by four volunteers rescued the entire archive in a weekend.
The stupendous waste involved was documented and never repaid.
The inquiry was stymied by files that had been legally destroyed in 2009.
One missing signature stymied a project worth several million.
His suavity at the reception concealed a genuine terror of small talk.
Suavity opens doors and, on its own, holds nothing behind them.

subaltern.definition: a subordinate, especially a junior officer
sentences: The subaltern's diary is a better source than any of the generals' memoirs.
In academic writing, subaltern means those excluded from the structures of power.
The score was subjective and four judges agreed on it exactly.
Pain is subjective, which makes it very hard to treat fairly.
The region was subjugated in three months and ungovernable for thirty years.
You can subjugate a population and never win a single argument.

sublimate.definition: to redirect an impulse into acceptable activity
sentences: He sublimated his frustration into a garden that won three prizes.
In chemistry, to sublimate is to go from solid to vapor without stopping at liquid.
The view from the ridge is sublime and the path to it is merely long.
From the sublime to the ridiculous is one step, Napoleon said, from experience.

subliminal.definition: below the level of conscious awareness
sentences: The subliminal advertising panic of the 1950s was based on a fabricated experiment.
The message was not subliminal; it was on the wall in yellow.
Every other consideration was subordinate to the deadline, which they missed anyway.
He treated the subordinate clause as an afterthought and lost the argument in it.

subpoena.definition: a legal order to appear or produce evidence
sentences: The subpoena produced four boxes of documents that had been described as lost.
Subpoena means "under penalty," which is exactly the tone of the document.
A subservient board approved everything and was surprised by the collapse.
Being subservient to the process rather than the purpose is a common failure.

subside.definition: to become less intense; to sink
sentences: The controversy subsided within a fortnight and left the policy in place.
The foundations subsided by four inches and the whole terrace followed.
A substantial minority objected, which the report described as "some concern."
The house needs substantial work, said the listing, meaning a new everything.
He could not substantiate the claim and repeated it in three interviews.
The allegation was substantiated by an expense record from 2011.

subsume.definition: to include within a larger category
sentences: The department was subsumed into a larger one and its name vanished within a year.
Two distinct problems were subsumed under one label and neither was solved.

subterfuge.definition: deception used to achieve a goal
sentences: The whole reorganization was subterfuge to remove one person without saying so.
Subterfuge requires effort that honesty would not have needed.
The change was subtle and everybody in the room noticed it at once.
A subtle argument survives scrutiny; a clever one usually does not.
The most subversive act available was reading the minutes aloud.
The novel was banned as subversive and is now a school text.
The exception subverted the rule so thoroughly that only the exception remained.
He subverted the process by following it exactly, which took nine months.
Each succeeding edition added a chapter and removed a footnote.
In succeeding years the policy was quietly reversed twice.
The succinct summary was the only page anyone read and it was enough.
Being succinct takes three drafts; being long-winded takes one.

succor.definition: help given in time of need
sentences: Succor arrived by boat nine hours after the road had gone under.
The charity offered succor and, more importantly, a working phone number.
The evidence was sufficient to convict and insufficient to convince the town.
Sufficient unto the day, says the proverb, meaning stop worrying about Thursday.
Universal suffrage arrived in stages, each described at the time as dangerously radical.
The suffrage campaign lasted six decades and is taught as though it took an afternoon.
A sullen silence followed the announcement and lasted until lunch.
The sullen sky over the harbor delivered nothing at all.

sully.definition: to damage the purity or reputation of
sentences: One accusation sullied a name that four decades of work had built.
He would not sully the record with a footnote he could not verify.
A sultry August emptied the city and filled every fountain with children.
The sultry heat before the storm made everyone irritable and then apologetic.

summit.definition: the highest point; a top-level meeting
sentences: The summit produced a photograph and a communiqué that agreed to meet again.
They reached the summit at dawn and could see nothing but cloud.
Sundry expenses accounted for a third of the budget and were itemized nowhere.
All and sundry turned up, which the caterers had not been warned about.

superannuated.definition: outdated or too old to be useful
sentences: The superannuated equipment worked perfectly and could not be insured.
He was described as superannuated at fifty-five and worked productively for thirty more years.
The orchestra played superbly to an audience of forty.
The building is superbly sited and indifferently built.
The supercilious waiter improved considerably when the bill was queried.
Supercilious comes from the raised eyebrow, which is exactly the gesture.

superficial.definition: shallow; concerned only with the surface
sentences: A superficial resemblance between the two cases misled the whole investigation.
The damage was superficial and the shock was not.
Every superfluous word was cut and the argument got twice as strong.
The second warning was superfluous; nobody had read the first.
The 2019 guidance supersedes the 2011 guidance, which four offices still use.
Supersede is spelled with an S in the middle, which almost nobody believes.
A supine regulator watched the industry write its own rules.
Supine literally means lying on your back, which is the image intended.
The younger technology supplanted the older one in about eighteen months.
He was supplanted by a deputy he had personally trained.
The leather stays supple if it is oiled twice a year and cracks if it is not.
A supple mind changes conclusions and keeps its standards.
The suppliant waited three hours and was granted four minutes.
Suppliants at the temple left offerings that archaeologists still count.
He supplicated for an extension and received one, ungraciously.
To supplicate is to beg on your knees, literally in the older sense.
The entire theory rests on a supposition nobody has tested.
It is pure supposition, he said, and repeated it as fact within a week.
A surfeit of information and a shortage of judgment describes the modern problem.
He died, the chronicle claims, of a surfeit of lampreys.
The surly barman poured an excellent pint in complete silence.
Surly service is forgiven where the food is good and nowhere else.
From the packing boxes she surmised the resignation two weeks early.
We may surmise what he thought; the letters do not say.
They surmounted every obstacle except the one in the funding agreement.
The tower is surmounted by a weathervane older than the church beneath it.
A surreptitious glance at his phone during the eulogy was noticed by everyone.
Surreptitious copying of the files took four months and one afternoon to discover.
Test scores became a surrogate for learning and then replaced it entirely.
The deputy acted as surrogate for eleven months and was never given the title.
The provenance was suspect and the auction went ahead regardless.
Any statistic that exactly confirms the speaker's position is suspect.
The sentence was suspended, which the headline reported as an acquittal.
The whole department was suspended in a state of waiting for eleven weeks.
The driver swerved to avoid a fox and hit a wall.
He never swerved from the argument he had made in his first paper.
They were swindled by a broker whose credentials nobody had checked.
The swindle worked because it offered a return that was almost plausible.
The sybarite of the group insisted on the hotel with actual pillows.
Sybaris was a Greek city so luxurious that its name became an insult.
The sycophants agreed with everything and warned him about nothing.
Every powerful person is surrounded by sycophants and complains about being misinformed.

syllogism.definition: a deductive argument in three parts
sentences: The classic syllogism runs: all men are mortal, Socrates is a man, therefore Socrates is mortal.
A valid syllogism with a false premise gives you a confident wrong answer.
The symbiosis between the university and the town survived four decades of complaint.
Lichen is a symbiosis so complete that it was mistaken for a single organism.
The symmetry of the facade hides a floor plan of complete chaos.
There is a pleasing symmetry in the two errors cancelling each other exactly.
The two failures were synchronous, which ruled out coincidence immediately.
Synchronous meetings cost everyone's time; the asynchronous kind cost only the writer's.
The syncopated rhythm is what makes the tune impossible to sit still through.
Syncopation puts the emphasis where the ear does not expect it.

synergy.definition: combined effect greater than the sum of parts
sentences: The promised synergy of the merger produced two redundancies and one very long integration.
Genuine synergy exists and is rarer than the word's use suggests.
The synoptic chapter is worth more to a beginner than the four detailed ones.
Synoptic weather charts show the whole system rather than one station's readings.

syntax.definition: the arrangement of words in sentences
sentences: The syntax is correct and the sentence still means nothing.
German syntax puts the verb at the end, which English speakers find suspenseful.

synthesize.definition: to combine parts into a whole
sentences: The review synthesizes forty studies into one usable conclusion.
Anyone can summarize; synthesizing requires deciding what matters.

table.definition: to submit for discussion, or to postpone
sentences: To table a motion means to propose it in Britain and to bury it in America.
The amendment was tabled and, depending on the country, either debated or forgotten.
There was a tacit agreement that nobody would mention the previous director.
Tacit knowledge is what an expert cannot write down and cannot work without.
The taciturn engineer spoke twice a meeting and was right both times.
Taciturn is silence by temperament, not by strategy.
It took tact to deliver the news and about four attempts to get the wording right.
Tact is knowing which true thing to leave unsaid.

tangent.definition: a sudden divergence from the topic
sentences: He went off on a tangent about ferries and never returned to the budget.
In geometry a tangent touches the curve once and departs, which is exactly right.
The objection was tangential and consumed the entire second hour.
A tangential remark occasionally turns out to be the important one.
After two years there was one tangible result and a great deal of process.
Tangible assets can be sold; the other kind can only be argued about.
The archive tantalized researchers with a catalogue and no access.
Tantalus stood in water he could not drink, which is where the word comes from.
A tantalizing fragment of the letter survives and the rest was used to light a fire.
The tantalizing smell from the kitchen made the speeches unbearable.
Silence in that meeting was tantamount to consent, as everyone understood.
The delay was tantamount to a refusal and was designed to be.

tarnish.definition: to dull or damage a reputation
sentences: One episode tarnished a reputation that decades of work had built.
Silver tarnishes in air, which is why the good cutlery lives in a drawer.
Do not tarry, said the note, which they did, and missed the ferry.
He tarried an hour over coffee and made the decision on the walk home.

tautology.definition: needless repetition of the same idea
sentences: "Free gift" is a tautology that has survived every editor in advertising.
The definition was a tautology: the rule applies wherever the rule applies.
The tawdry finale undid two hours of genuine subtlety.
Tawdry comes from cheap lace sold at St Audrey's fair.
The schedule was taxing enough that two people left before the launch.
A taxing conversation is one where every sentence must be weighed.
The tedious checking is exactly the part that prevents the interesting disaster.
He was tedious about wine and delightful about everything else.

teem.definition: to be full of; to swarm
sentences: The rock pool teems with things that are invisible until you sit still.
The city teemed with visitors and every one of them wanted the same photograph.
The most telling detail was who had not been invited.
A telling silence in a negotiation is worth studying afterward.
The telltale ink stain on his cuff placed him in the room.
Telltale cracks in the plaster were photographed for two years before anyone acted.
She had the temerity to ask what the department actually did.
Temerity is courage judged by someone who disapproves of it.
Temper the criticism with one honest compliment and it may be heard.
Steel is tempered by heat and cooling, which makes it flexible rather than brittle.
The temperance movement built libraries as an alternative to public houses.
Temperance in argument is rarer and more useful than temperance at dinner.
His temperate response to a hostile review won him more allies than the review cost.
The temperate climate is why the island grows both apples and complaints about weather.
Their optimism was tempered by four consecutive failed attempts.
Tempered glass shatters into blunt pieces, which is the entire point of it.
Their tempestuous partnership produced four albums and no working friendship.
A tempestuous meeting is occasionally more productive than a polite one.

temporal.definition: relating to time or worldly affairs
sentences: The bishop's temporal power exceeded his spiritual authority by some distance.
The temporal order of the events was disputed for a decade.
